protocol.cache: fresh backend/output caches each run; warm OS filesystem cache; fixed TAST
protocol.comparison: Release generated Go file hashes equal between JS and Go hosts; Dev stable independently; no application test suite rerun
protocol.rust: Not measured. User requested estimates from per-project historical Rust/Go ratios after cancelling Rust bootstrap.

go_dependencies.module_manifests: same pinned go.mod/go.sum as normal b8x runner
go_dependencies.go_export_cache: shared between runs, warmed by warmup; backend caches empty each run

protocol.revision: All Go/Dev invocations rerun with explicit GOGC=off/GOMEMLIMIT=16GiB; all corrected JS invocations retained unchanged from v2. Native rounds retain the Go/Dev relative order from v2, with JS entries skipped.

rust_estimation.formula: new Go Release median_ms * historical Rust ms / historical Go ms, independently per project
rust_estimation.totals: sums of unrounded per-project estimates; no global historical ratio
rust_estimation.assumption: The historical Rust/Go relative compilation speed remains applicable to the current compiler.

excluded_attempts.reason: Warmup JS failed after SIGQUIT of helper blocked in io.ReadAll(stdin); Node parent waiting in spawnSync. No timing retained. Exact-request replay passed 8 times; frozen compiler unchanged.
All old JS pipe-transport runs replaced after two intermittent stdin waits; successful Go/Dev runs retained unchanged.

All 408 prior Go/Dev invocations replaced because launcher hardware detection can be unavailable in the sandbox, leaving GC policy unverified. V3 explicitly sets GOGC=off and GOMEMLIMIT=16GiB. The 204 corrected JS invocations are retained unchanged.

limitations: Rust values are calculated estimates; no new Rust timings or output validation support this column.
Historical ratios come from approximate published values and may not transfer to the current compiler.

The historical 4–5 October backend timings and this campaign cover different work: current cold builds also prepare Go dependency exports and packages, and publish persistent incremental caches and source proofs. The historical difference does not isolate a compiler regression or quantify the cost of incremental support.
Compiler revisions, input corpora, Go-host memory policy and sample counts also differ from the historical campaign; no controlled old/new comparison under one protocol was performed.
No application test suite rerun for this measurement campaign.
Warm operating-system filesystem cache; no explicit CPU affinity.

All JS invocations use the transport-only corrected bundle and are retained from v2. All Go/Dev invocations were then replaced under explicit GOGC=off/GOMEMLIMIT=16GiB because sandboxed hardware detection left the previous memory policy unverified. The hosts were not measured in one uninterrupted interleaved run.
